writing.patterns: Most of your writing is specs, stakeholder updates and launch notes. Early on you asked for a draft and edited it; lately you write the rough version and ask what's unclear.
writing.helps: AI gets you from notes to a readable page fast, and it's a patient reader for a second pass.
writing.risk: When AI drafts, its structure becomes yours. Your updates can end up sounding like everyone else's.
writing.try: Write the one sentence the reader must take away before you ask for anything.

research.patterns: You hand AI the first sweep: competitors, patterns, what's been written on a topic. You decide what's worth following up.
research.helps: A fast map of unfamiliar ground, so your own reading starts in the right place.
research.risk: AI's summary can quietly decide what counts as important before you've looked yourself.
research.try: Pick one claim from the summary and trace it to the source before you use it.

coding.patterns: Side projects, mostly prototypes. AI writes most of the code; you say what it should do and notice when it doesn't.
coding.helps: You can build things you couldn't before, and test an idea in an evening instead of a sprint.
coding.risk: When AI also fixes what it broke, you learn the outcome but not the code.
coding.try: Before asking for a fix, write one line on what you think is wrong.

design.patterns: AI makes the first layout and you rework it. Your strongest moves come when you reject the first version and say why.
design.helps: Something concrete on the canvas in minutes, so the conversation is about the design and not a blank page.
design.risk: Accepting the first structure too quickly makes the work look like a template.
design.try: When a first pass feels off, name the principle it misses before asking for another.

presenting.patterns: You know the story already. You use AI for order, framing and trimming the deck to time.
presenting.helps: It helps turn a pile of points into a sequence an audience can follow.
presenting.risk: If AI sets the flow, the talk can sound smooth without sounding like your argument.
presenting.try: Write the one-line takeaway first, then ask AI to test the deck against it.

career.patterns: Portfolio case studies, a promotion doc, a few hard messages. You let AI set the tone more here than anywhere else.
career.helps: A calm second opinion when the stakes feel high and the words won't come.
career.risk: Polish can drift into generic polish when sounding right matters more than sounding like you.
career.try: Mark the sentence that sounds most like you and ask AI to keep that voice.

personal.patterns: This is where you use AI least like a tool: thinking out loud about decisions, plans and the odd question.
personal.helps: Room to think without turning everything into an output.
personal.risk: Because it feels like a conversation, weak advice slips by more easily.
personal.try: When it matters, ask what you'd still believe if AI hadn't answered.

studying.patterns: Learning just enough front-end to build your prototypes. You ask for explanations, then try it yourself.
studying.helps: Explanations pitched at your level, with examples from the thing you're actually building.
studying.risk: Reading an explanation can feel like understanding before you've used it.
studying.try: After an explanation, close it and write the example yourself before asking more.

dimensions.ideas: AI used to bring most of the starting ideas. Now you more often arrive with one and use AI to widen it.
dimensions.direction: You steer. Where a chat goes is usually set by your redirects, not by AI's suggestions.
dimensions.research: AI brings most of the facts and references; you add the context it couldn't know, like users, stakeholders and constraints.
dimensions.building: AI still makes most first drafts, code and layouts, but more of them now start from something you wrote.
dimensions.problems: You catch more of what's wrong than you used to, especially tone, hierarchy and fit.
dimensions.final_call: What ships is your call. AI rarely settles a decision for you.
dimensions.checking: You question and test AI's answers about half the time, more than early on.
dimensions.understanding: You mostly ask for the answer, but asks for critique of your own work are growing.

all.summary: A year ago you asked AI to draft and then edited. Now you more often write first and **ask AI to push back**.

you.title: The Art Director
you.body: You know what good looks like before you can make it. Your best moments are when you say **why** something isn't working.

ai.title: The Fast Maker
ai.body: AI turns your direction into drafts, layouts and code quickly, then waits for you to reshape them.

together.title: Sketch. Critique. Ship.
together.body: AI gets a first version into the room; your critique decides what it becomes.

all.whats_working: You've moved from reacting to AI's drafts to giving AI something to react to. Your critiques are more specific than they were in the autumn.
all.prompt_better: You often ask for "another version" without saying what to keep. Try: "keep the hierarchy, simplify the copy, same tone as my first draft."
all.watch_for: AI still builds most of what you ship. That's fine for speed, but your own first-draft muscles get less practice than your critique does.

claude_ai.summary: In chats you've shifted from "write this for me" to **"here's my draft, what's unclear?"**

you.title: The Editor
you.body: You're strongest once there's a page to react to, and lately that page is more often **your own**.

ai.title: The Research Assistant
ai.body: AI does the first sweep of reading and the first pass of wording, then hands it back.

together.title: Draft. Question. Tighten.
together.body: The page goes back and forth until it says what you meant, in fewer words.

claude_ai.whats_working: Asking for critique of your own drafts gets you sharper writing than editing AI's did.
claude_ai.prompt_better: Say who the reader is. "For an engineering lead who skims" gets a better critique than "make this clearer."
claude_ai.watch_for: In research, AI's summary often becomes the reading. Check one source yourself before you build on it.

claude_code.summary: Claude Code lets you build working prototypes on your own. You set what it should do; **AI writes nearly all the code**.

you.title: The Product Owner
you.body: You know exactly how the prototype should feel and you notice when it doesn't. The code itself you mostly leave to AI.

ai.title: The Engineer
ai.body: AI writes, runs and fixes the code, and explains it when you ask.

together.title: Describe. Try. Fix.
together.body: You describe, AI builds, you click around and report what's wrong.

claude_code.whats_working: You test by using the thing, and you're quick to say when the behaviour is wrong.
claude_code.prompt_better: Give AI the user's goal, not just the change: "a first-time user should find export without scrolling."
claude_code.watch_for: When AI also diagnoses and fixes its own bugs, you get the result without the understanding. Ask why before accepting a fix now and then.

dimensions.ideas: What to build is usually your idea; how to build it is AI's.
dimensions.research: AI brings nearly all the technical know-how; you bring what the prototype is for.
dimensions.building: AI writes almost all the code. You change little directly, but more often than you did in January.
dimensions.problems: Bugs get caught about evenly: you notice when it behaves wrong, AI finds out why.
dimensions.understanding: You mostly ask for the fix, not the why, and a little more so lately.

claude_design.summary: In Claude Design, AI makes the first layout and **you decide what's right**.

you.title: The Critic
you.body: You spot what's off in a layout fast and you say so. Most finished designs carry **your** edits.

ai.title: The Mockup Machine
ai.body: AI turns a sentence into a screen in seconds, so there's always something to react to.

together.title: Generate. Judge. Refine.
together.body: AI makes options, you pick one and push it until it feels right.

claude_design.whats_working: You catch hierarchy and spacing problems AI misses, and you fix them yourself instead of asking.
claude_design.prompt_better: Start with constraints: "one primary action, mobile first, our type scale." Fewer variants to throw away.
claude_design.watch_for: Starting from AI's layout means you rarely explore a direction it wouldn't suggest. Sketch one yourself first now and then.

dimensions.ideas: The core idea is usually yours; AI fills in the layout options around it.
dimensions.problems: You spot most of what's wrong in a layout yourself.
dimensions.checking: You question AI's layouts more often than you take them as they are.
dimensions.understanding: You ask why a layout works about as often as you just ask for the next one.
